directive.quote: Every engine job of the old Worker's rust-engine backlog rows works on the new engine, one to one or better.

preserve: an AI app whose connector screen asks for a client id gets a client with a fixed, published id
a fixed client has no secret (token_endpoint_auth_method none) and S256 PKCE, and only the exact redirect addresses in its row
it never expires, and a registration never takes or overwrites its id
authorize and token read it exactly where they read every registered client
allowed_deltas: a fixed client is the account's own row, added by its owner through the door (sign-in:add-client, sign-in:clients, sign-in:remove-client) with the id the owner chooses, instead of deploy data for everyone (records/oauth-client-records.json): every OAuth client here is a per-account row (client_of) and the engine keeps nothing centrally (PRINCIPLES 3)

the shipped row for one vendor's app and its name are not carried: no vendor name in engine code or data (PRINCIPLES 2); records/oauth-client-records.json is not a source of this contract for that reason
the owner may remove a fixed client, which ends its grant; the old deploy row could only change with a deploy
the OAUTH_KV wrapper and its one-minute token memory (withFixedClients, envWithFixedClients, kept-reads) drop out: Worker plumbing
banned_substitutions: a central or deploy-wide client table
a vendor's name or app in engine code or data
a fixed client with a secret or a pattern redirect
